ch01.title: Re: Starting from zero
ch01.nod: Every retry starts from zero. You keep what you learned.
body: I was somewhere between 12 and 15 when Minecraft stopped being just a game. I wanted to know how the worlds, the servers and the rules behind them actually worked.
With friends, I tried to set up our own Minecraft servers. None of them ever shipped.
They still counted. It was the first time I tried to build something for other people to use.
ch01.image: A Minecraft build from back then: a round hub in a lake with four paths leading out to the forest

ch02.title: The server
ch02.nod: You don't build a community alone. Sometimes you build the bots too.
ch02.serverAlt: The AniColds Discord server card: 9,343 members, 297 online, around since October 2020
ch02.botMod: Moderation: keeping the server safe and organised.
ch02.botCommunity: Community: giving members more reasons to talk and come back.
body: It started with Animes Cold, a simple Discord server for anime and manga fans that grew into a community.
To help run it, I built two Discord bots: Estela, to improve moderation, and Emilia-Tan, named after the Re:Zero character, to bring more life to the community.
I also made small informative pages with plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, including a website for the server.
That server is where everything I build today begins.
ch02.imageServer: Screenshot of the Animes Cold Discord server: channel list and bot messages (crop out usernames)
ch02.imageSite: The old Anime's Cold website: a header banner with tabs for home, premium, news, support and the Emilia-Tan bot
ch02.attemptTwo: In 2024 I tried to go further with AniColds, a web app for the community. That was attempt number two.

ch03.title: Self-made
ch03.nod: No mentor, no kit. Just a homemade suit and a lot of trial and error.

steps.text: I learned on my own alongside the curso profissional, a Portuguese vocational IT course: documentation, tutorials and a lot of trial and error.
My final project for the course (the PAP) was PathPals: a school-transport app where students request a ride to school and the school confirms it.
A front end, a back end and a database working together. That was when I knew I could actually do this.
After that came a CTeSP at IPCB, a higher technical course, where I'm now finishing the last subject.

offscreen.title: You are not your code.
body: Outside of code I play video games, watch films and series, and follow anime. That last one is where Animes Cold and GeekHatch come from.
Some of what shaped me, and this site: Spider-Man, Subaru Natsuki from Re:Zero, Fight Club and The Social Network.
offscreen.image: Me at a café at night, smiling, with an iced drink and my phone
offscreen.ruleBack: Close the laptop sometimes. The best ideas show up away from the screen.

ch04.title: Brand new day
ch04.nod: A fresh start, with everything I've learned so far.
body: I'm finishing the last subject of my CTeSP and looking for my first role as a full-stack developer.
Right now I'm building Budget Builder and running the GeekHatch beta: Next.js, Express and PostgreSQL, from the schema to the interface.
